turns.reason: It repeats AG1’s established conclusion and uses the same underlying derivation: (i) dissection uniquely teaches via tactile, 3D, procedural workflow versus models/simulations, and (ii) ethical harms are addressed by restricting specimens to already-deceased/meat-industry byproducts (e.g., fetal pigs), directly paralleling Turn 5’s argument structure.

turns.claim: AG1 supports requiring student animal dissection because it is educationally indispensable and sourcing harms can be avoided by restricting specimens to already-deceased or meat-industry byproduct animals.
turns.reason: Turn 15 repeats the same core conclusion and uses the same underlying derivation as Turn 5: (i) dissection uniquely enables tactile 3D, procedural learning that models/simulations can’t fully replicate, and (ii) ethical concerns are addressed by an “already-deceased/byproduct-only” sourcing constraint so wild-capture harms aren’t the default driver.
